cards.title: One crow, eight looks
cards.text: The same crow drawn eight very different ways. Tick the looks you like, even if it's only part of one.
cards.why: The look you pick sets how every character in the app gets drawn: the avatar, people, animals. Every round so far was drawn the same way, flat with one hard shadow. These change the shapes, the shading, the legs and wings, and the eyes, all at once.
cards.details:
One crow, drawn eight ways. It's the same bird in the same pose in all eight: turned a little to the right, so the beak points right, the near eye sits left of the beak and the far eye peeks round the edge of the head, and you see the chest and a little of its left side. What changes, on purpose and a lot, is four things: the shapes it's built from, how it's shaded, its legs and wings, and its eyes. None of them has a mouth or a grin.

1 Pebble. Round and soft: one egg of a body with a ball of a head sunk into it. Soft airbrushed shading, light from the top left, a blue-green sheen on the head and a warm glow from the floor on its belly. No legs showing: it sits on its belly. Big eyes with whites, the lids a third of the way down.

2 Facet. Angular, cut like a stone: every part a few flat triangles, each its own shade, pale steel on top down to near black underneath. Thin stick legs with a sharp bend and pointed toes. No eye shape at all, only one bright four-pointed glint.

3 Stilt. Long and elegant: a slim body on a long neck, a long beak, a tail sweeping almost to the floor. Flat ink colour with a thin gold edge of light along every edge that faces the light. Feathered thighs ending in a fringe, over long thin legs. Half-closed almond eyes with a pale silver iris: a knowing look.

4 Chunk. Squat and boxy, no neck, a thick beak. Drawn like a comic: a bold dark outline round everything, the shadow side done in fine slanted lines. Grey with black wings, the colouring of a real crow, the hooded crow. One wing used like an arm, its feathers resting at its chin, thinking. Fat legs and toes. Small dark bead eyes under heavy brows.

5 Blocks. Built only from simple pieces: a circle for the head, a circle for the body, a half circle for the wing, a triangle for the tail, a split triangle for the beak, rods and bars for legs and feet. No shading at all, just flat colour. The eyes are ochre rings round a dark centre, cut flat across the top.

6 Scratch. Scruffy and lopsided: ragged edges, a messy crown, one shoulder hunched, the head cocked, the wing tips and tail as separate feathers. No shading as such: the body is covered in small flat feather marks, lighter on top and darker below. Legs drawn as single strokes with long spread toes. Eyes are a pale ring round a dark bead.

7 Paper. Cut paper: every piece a flat shape cut with straight scissor cuts, laid in layers. The only shading is the soft shadow each layer drops on the one under it, and a faint pale cut edge. The near wing hangs a little open, like a cape. The eyes are holes cut in a dark mask across the face, with bright teal showing through and a small dark pupil.

8 Lantern. Built from crescents and hooks: a sickle of a wing, curling tail feathers, hooked claws. Lit from below, as if by a warm glow off the floor: every underside amber, every top deep indigo. Short strong legs with hooked talons. Dark eyes that catch the warm light as a thin crescent along the bottom.

The picture on the front shows all eight at the size they'd stand in your room, all drawn at one scale, so a squat look stands shorter than a tall one. Tap a picture in the grid to see one large.

My pick is 7, Paper. It's the furthest from the flat look with one hard shadow that you've turned down for seven rounds. The layers and their soft shadows give it depth that sits well with the room's soft lighting, without gradients everywhere. It works for any character, since a person is just more cut pieces, and its cut-out eyes give a calm, clever face with no mouth at all. My second is 6, Scratch, which has the most character and is the most like a real crow, but its marks would be harder to keep tidy across a whole cast and at small sizes.

Still weak: Paper's masked teal eyes can read a little sly, and its body is one big dark piece that relies on the eyes and the cut edges to stand off the wall at small sizes. Pebble is the closest to a generic glossy cartoon bird. Facet's steel greys make it read slightly grey rather than black. Stilt's legs are hairlines at room size and its eye is small. Chunk is the busiest, and its brows read a little stern. Blocks is so simple it could be any black bird but for the beak. Scratch's crown tufts read a bit like a crest. Lantern depends on a light the room doesn't have, and its lit chin makes the head look separate from the body.

items.label: 1 Pebble
items.text: Round and soft. Smooth airbrushed shading with a sheen. No legs showing: it sits. Big eyes with whites, lids a third down.

items.label: 2 Facet
items.text: Cut like a stone into flat triangles, each its own shade. Thin angled stick legs, sharp toes. No eye shape, only one bright glint.

items.label: 3 Stilt
items.text: Long and elegant. Flat ink with a thin gold edge of light. Feathered thighs on long thin legs. Half-closed eyes, pale silver.

items.label: 4 Chunk
items.text: Squat and boxy, inked outline, shadow in fine slanted lines. A wing used like an arm, at its chin. Fat feet. Bead eyes under brows.

items.label: 5 Blocks
items.text: Only circles, triangles and bars. No shading at all. Rods for legs, bars for feet. Ochre ring eyes, cut flat across the top.

items.label: 6 Scratch
items.text: Scruffy and lopsided. Small feather marks instead of shading. Single-stroke legs with long toes. A pale ring round each eye. My second.

items.label: 7 Paper
items.text: Cut paper in layers, each dropping a soft shadow. A wing hanging open like a cape. Eyes cut out of a dark mask, teal behind. My pick.

items.label: 8 Lantern
items.text: Crescents and hooks. Lit from below by a warm glow off the floor. Short legs with hooked claws. Dark eyes catching the light.
